interfaces.name: Evernote GUI clients (web, desktop, mobile)
interfaces.technology: Web app, Windows/macOS desktop apps, iOS/Android apps
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating views, menus, and forms over a persistent, navigable representation of the note collection. Affordance Manipulation.

provenance.evidence: First-party clients for Windows, Mac, iOS, Android and the web app.
Confirms first-party Desktop and Web clients as the interactive surface.

interfaces.name: Web Clipper
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party browser-extension capture surface; the consumer manipulates capture affordances (clip type, notebook, tags, annotations). Affordance Manipulation.

provenance.evidence: Web Clipper integrates with the account and is compatible with all major browsers.
Provider page describing the first-party clipper client.

interfaces.name: AI Assistant
interfaces.technology: In-app chat drawer (LLM-backed, built with OpenAI)
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer interacts through natural-language messages; the assistant's search, creation, tagging, and web lookup are orchestrated internally and are not part of the consumer-facing contract. Contextual Conversation.

provenance.evidence: Chat drawer opened from a button in the desktop and web app; assistant reads, searches, and works with the user's notes.
AI Assistant responds to a simple request and retrieves content directly from the chat window.

interfaces.name: Evernote MCP server
interfaces.classification_rationale: Provider-hosted gateway exposing Read and Create capabilities that external AI agents discover and invoke; capability discovery and selection structure the contract. MCP boundary case resolves to Agentic.

provenance.evidence: Evernote hosts an MCP server acting as a secure gateway with Read and Create capabilities, available to all paid users; updated August 2026.

interfaces.name: Cloud API (EDAM)
interfaces.technology: Thrift-based RPC over HTTPS (NoteStore, UserStore), OAuth
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined operations against the Evernote web service through structured RPC calls. Operation Invocation.

provenance.evidence: The Cloud API speaks directly to the Evernote web service to act on a single user's account; new key issuance is gated behind manual review.
API Reference generated from Evernote source describes the core API types and functions.

interfaces.name: Local API
interfaces.classification_rationale: Provider-defined operations on the local client invoked through structured commands, with a different base and auth model than the Cloud API. Operation Invocation.

provenance.evidence: Calls the local clients using command lines on Windows, AppleScript on Mac, and Intents on Android, with security handled by the local application.

interfaces.name: Email-to-Evernote
interfaces.technology: Inbound email to a unique @m.evernote.com address
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer submits a structured message to a provider-defined address to invoke note creation, with subject-line commands directing notebook, tags, and reminders. Operation Invocation, analogous to SMTP submission.

provenance.evidence: Forwarding an email to the unique Evernote address creates a note; subject-line commands specify notebook, tags, and reminders.
Each account has an automatically generated unique incoming email address.

interfaces.name: Webhooks
interfaces.technology: HTTP callbacks to a consumer-controlled URL
interfaces.classification_rationale: The service initiates a call to a consumer-controlled URL when subscribed note events occur, filtered by a note filter. Event Notification.

provenance.evidence: A webhook is registered with the customer key, target URL, and a note filter; the service then calls that URL on matching note events.

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: No first-party TUI; no CLI to carry one.
No official evidence; the public API is Thrift-based (EDAM).

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: SDKs (iOS, Android, Python, Java, and others)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Client libraries that implement the Cloud API, not interfaces.
Features inside the GUI and AI Assistant, not separate access interfaces.
Built on the Cloud API; not provider-defined interfaces.
